title: Heterogeneous kernel fusion and shadow-KV prefetch for Mistral edge handling
author: Jun Park
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) add hetero fusion policy and unit tests; 2) shadow-KV manager with prefetch heuristics and runtime flag; 3) polish: metrics, canary rollout flag, docs and benchmark harness updates
description: Summary: This change introduces two coordinated runtime features targeted at Mistral MQA/GQA quirks: (1) a heterogeneous kernel fusion policy that lets the dispatcher choose fused kernels by head-group shape and stride characteristics, and (2) a shadow-KV prefetch manager that speculatively materializes small KV windows for likely-needed slabs on multi-query workloads. Motivation: Mistral MQA workloads show head-wise asymmetry and frequent small-span KV access patterns that lead to suboptimal kernel selection and repeated memory fetches. On certain sequence-length distributions we observed 10-20% higher p95 latency compared to fused-kernel paths used for dense heads. Design: Hetero fusion: a lightweight policy module analyzes runtime head stride and per-request shape metadata to select a fused-kernel variant or fall back to baseline kernels. Fusion decisions are cached per-model-version for the session and invalidated on rollout. Shadow-KV prefetch: the manager maintains a per-request shadow KV buffer (bounded, preallocated slab) that prefetches likely next-window keys based on last N-step head access history. Prefetch heuristics include head-affinity scoring, recent-token locality, and explicit model hints delivered via model metadata. Safety and fallback: both features have runtime config flags and a safe-mode that disables fusion/prefetch for models marked with known quirk tags. The dispatcher falls back to standard kernel paths if fusion fails or if contention rises. Observability: new metrics (fusion_path_hit, shadow_kv_prefetch_hits, prefetch_evictions, fusion_decisions_by_model) and traces for prefetch latency were added. Performance: microbenchmarks on our MQA synthetic harness show median p50 improvements of 8% and p95 gains up to 14% on Mistral 7B MQA with bursty short bursts (seq<=64). For mixed consumer workloads the continuous-batching throughput improved 7% and per-token CPU/GPU utilization smoothing reduced tail jitter. Cost impact: preliminary infra runs indicate a 6-10% effective token cost reduction for high-mqa traffic after feature rollouts. Testing: added unit tests for fusion policy decision logic and shadow-KV eviction semantics; added an end-to-end microbench that exercises continuous batching interaction. CI flakiness: one flaky test in scheduler was fixed by stricter order guarantees and a small sleep removed from the test harness. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime feature flag hetero_fusion_v1 and shadow_kv_prefetch_v1. Canary rollout plan: enable for 5% of traffic on dedicated pools first, monitor metrics for increased memory pressure, fusion_path_hit ratio, and end-to-end latency regressions. If regressions exceed thresholds (p95 latency +10% or memory pressure +15%) automatically disable. Related work: follows ENG-8342 (kernel dispatch refactor) and ENG-8397 (mqa evaluation harness). Checklist: - [x] Design doc added - docs/notes/hetero-fusion-design.md - [x] Unit + integration tests - tests/perf/mistral_mqa_microbench.py - [x] Metrics and traces - [x] Feature flags and config - config/feature_flags.yaml - [x] Benchmark results attached to Linear ticket. Commits: commit a3f5c9b - hetero fusion policy initial implementation; commit b4d2f11 - shadow-KV manager and heuristics; commit c7e8d44 - metrics, docs, and fixes. Review notes: see reviewer comments below.
review_conversation: Ayesha Patel (reviewer) - 2026-03-05: Nice approach. Two asks: 1) can you add a guard so shadow-KV prefetch doesn't allocate for requests under X tokens to avoid memory blowups; 2) can we expose a percentiles histogram for fusion decision latency?

Jun Park (author) - 2026-03-05: Responding: 1) added a min_prefetch_seq_len cutoff (configurable) and capped shadow buffer per-request; 2) added fusion_decision_latency histogram to runtime metrics. Updated tests to cover small-request path.
Marco Santos (reviewer) - 2026-03-06: Implementation looks good. One question on determinism in the fusion cache invalidation across rollouts. Could cause mismatch across replicas during canary.

Jun Park (author) - 2026-03-06: Good catch. Made cache shard-local and added a rollout epoch tag to the cache key so invalidation happens uniformly when model version or rollout epoch changes. Added a unit test for invalidation semantics.
Liang Chen (reviewer) - 2026-03-07: CI initially failed on a flaky scheduler test. After re-run CI passed. Please ensure the scheduler sleep removal is safe on older kernels.
Jun Park (author) - 2026-03-07: Confirmed removal is safe; added an explicit ordering guarantee in the scheduler and note in changelog.
Ayesha Patel (approver) - 2026-03-08: Approved. Observability looks sufficient for canary.
ci_summary: Presubmit: lint OK, unit tests OK, perf microbench run (internal) OK. CI flaky scheduler test failed once and was rerun; final status PASS.
release_notes: Introduce heterogenous kernel fusion and shadow-KV prefetch to reduce latency and improve throughput for Mistral MQA/GQA workloads. Feature gated; disabled by default. Monitor fusion and prefetch metrics during canary.
notes: This PR is focused on runtime improvements and does not change external APIs. Ops: add hetero_fusion_v1 and shadow_kv_prefetch_v1 flags to production config when ready to roll out.
